about: DNA-origami designs of the Nanorulers specimen (BSD-3-Clause). tools/gen_origami_designs.mjs validates them and builds the JS reference's table (web/prototype/scope/origami_designs_data.js), the core's (core/src/origami_designs.inc) and the viewer's (web/origami_designs.js); never edit those by hand. A design's index here is the core param origamiDesign.

A design is the molecule at rest: a body in its own straight frame (x along the length, y across it in the coverslip plane, h the height relative to the body's mid-plane), the spots of docking strands on it, how it deforms (wlc2d: the centreline is a 2D surface-equilibrated worm-like chain of persistence length Lp, cross-sections stay straight and normal to it; rigid: none) and how it lands (roll about its own axis: uniform or fixed; flat: a plate lies face up; the height of the body's bottom above the glass).

Spots sit on a lattice whose step is the param origamiSpacingNm (one value for every design; 80 nm by default), and the body grows with it. A rod ('cylinder') has its spots at 'at' = 0, 1, 2, ... lattice steps along its axis and endNm of rod beyond the first and last spot: length = (last - first) x spacing + 2 endNm. A plate ('plate') carries a lattice: 'hex' = flat-topped hexagons, neighbour centres one spacing apart, columns spacing x sqrt(3)/2 apart, odd columns half a step down ('odd-q-down'), cells named 'CCRR' (column, row from the top-left, as a hex-map editor labels them); the plate is the bounding box of all cols x rows hexagons (+ marginNm), and each listed cell holds one docking strand at its centre on the top face.

Per molecule: rest sites -> incorporation (the label's labelling %) -> deformation -> landing (roll, heights) -> placement (position, yaw) -> emitters; every step a pure function of (seed, address). 'deformation' and 'landing' values are the suggested defaults of the origami* params (the params win; a plate ignores the roll params).

Implemented: bodies 'cylinder' and 'plate', deformation 'wlc2d' (cylinders) and 'rigid', roll 'uniform' and 'fixed' (cylinders) and 'flat' (plates), cylinder spots with a ring, plate lattice 'hex'. Reserved, validated as not implemented: bodies 'cuboid', 'mesh'; deformation 'wlc3d', 'plate'; stiffnessVariation and curvaturePerUm != 0; explicit strand lists ('strands').

designs.name: 1D origami: nanoruler (3 spots)
designs.notes: The typical nanoruler body, a 12-helix bundle 13 nm in diameter (scheckenbach2020), as a cylinder, with three spots of docking strands one lattice spacing apart and 20 nm of rod beyond the outer ones: at the default 80 nm spacing a 200 nm rod with spots at 20, 100 and 180 nm from one end; five strand positions per spot, 72 deg apart on the surface (a modelling choice, not a product's specification). Persistence length 1500 nm: an estimate, softer than the 3-8.2 um measured for eight-helix bundles (chhabra2020). Geometry and bending: tools/origami_reference/origami_bend.py.

designs.name: 2D origami: TU Delft logo
designs.notes: The TU Delft logo (flame, T, U, D as an o) drawn as 37 cells of a 17 x 11 hex map, one docking strand at the centre of each, neighbouring centres one lattice spacing apart. A single-layer sheet, rigid and lying face up (never mirrored); 2 nm thick (about one helix diameter: an estimate). The sheet covers the whole hex map.
